title: GcpConfig
description: Configuration for the GCP cloud-burst Provisioner backend (ARC-13 / ADR-20, #378): where on Google Cloud to burst ephemeral compute nodes, how to size and price them, and how each node joins the cluster. Mirrors the Azure reference (azure_config.schema.json) via the CLI pattern. Mirrored by zetta::GcpConfig in include/zetta/gcp_provisioner.hpp and enforced by GcpConfig::from_json() in src/core/gcp_provisioner.cpp — keep them in sync. No cloud SDK lives behind the provisioner; this config is interpreted by a GcpControlPlane (the reference GcpCliControlPlane shells out to the `gcloud` CLI, the Managed Instance Group + Spot shape). A malformed config is rejected at the boundary so a misconfigured burst fails fast instead of bringing up the wrong (or no) fleet.

project_id.description: The GCP project the burst pool is created in.

zone.description: The Compute Engine zone the Managed Instance Group runs in (e.g. 'us-central1-a').

pool_name.description: Name of the burst pool (the Managed Instance Group). Stable so create + delete are idempotent. Defaults to 'zetta-burst' when omitted.

instance_template.description: The Compute Engine instance template the MIG instantiates. Defaults to 'zetta-burst-template'; the control plane ensures it exists (machine type / image / network / service account / Spot / startup-script) before creating the MIG.

machine_type.description: The Compute Engine machine type each node uses (e.g. 'a2-highgpu-1g', 'e2-standard-4'). Empty lets the control plane map the requested NodeCapability spec to a machine type.

image.description: The image family burst nodes boot from (e.g. 'debian-12'). Empty uses the control plane's default image.

network.description: The VPC network burst nodes attach to (e.g. 'default'). Empty uses the project default.

subnetwork.description: The subnetwork within the region burst nodes attach to. Empty uses the auto subnet for the network.

service_account.description: The service account email granted to burst nodes (the cloud-native side of the per-node burst identity).

spot.description: Burst Spot (preemptible) capacity — cheaper, interruptible — rather than standard on-demand nodes (gcloud --provisioning-model=SPOT).

seed_peer.description: The cluster seed address (host:port) injected into each node's startup-script metadata so it auto-joins the existing peer cluster at boot. Empty when the join address is supplied another way.
